N_eq stays bounded on the order of K and N_ref (tens up to ~100)
N_eq varies smoothly and continuously with both c and r
As r grows large, N_eq approaches the local growth target near K (dispersal weight r/(r+r_half) saturates)
As c -> 0 dispersal exchange vanishes and N_eq -> K

rationale: Structure from analyze_expression: explicit, no derivatives/integrals, explicitly solvable for N_eq. N_eq is the dependent variable; c (connectivity) and r (per-capita growth) are the two natural sampling axes (both labeled inputs and both drive the expression, r especially through the new r/(r+r_half) weighting). All 13 remaining free symbols are fixed parameters. Parameter magnitudes chosen at physically sensible biological scales (K=100 carrying capacity, N_ref=80 neighbor pool, sub-unity half-saturations and dispersal rate); r_half=0.5 and g_stay=1 lie within the suggested ranges. auto_balance converged with no coefficient changes and excitation_check confirms every term (and the new term at 57x sigma) is well above the noise floor.

scenario_text: A population is distributed across habitat patches connected by dispersal, and local density affects how individuals spread outward. Steady-state abundance in a focal patch depends on the balance between local growth and net dispersal exchange with neighbors. Investigators measure equilibrium local density across patches of differing connectivity. This benchmark isolates dispersal-driven spatial equilibrium.
